title: Valid Parentheses
description: Given a string s containing only the characters '()[]{}', determine whether the string is a valid parentheses sequence: every closing bracket must match the most recent unmatched opening bracket of the same type and all brackets must be closed. Constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 10^4.

title: Subarray Sum Equals K
description: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the number of contiguous non-empty subarrays whose sum equals k. Array length is up to 2*10^4 and elements can be negative, so an O(n) solution using extra space is desirable.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
description: Given an array prices where prices[i] is the stock price on day i, find the maximum profit from one buy-sell transaction (buy before sell) and return 0 if no positive profit is possible. With 1 <= prices.length <= 1e5 and prices up to 1e4, an O(n) single-pass solution is appropriate.

title: Two Sum
description: Given an array of integers and a target integer, return the indices of the two distinct numbers that add up to the target. You may assume exactly one valid solution exists and cannot reuse the same element; array length is up to 10^4 and values/target fit in 32-bit signed range.

title: Trapping Rain Water
description: Given an array of non-negative integers representing bar heights (width = 1), compute the total units of water that can be trapped after raining between the bars. Key constraints: n up to 2*10^4 and height[i] up to 10^5, so an O(n) time / O(1) space solution is desirable.

title: Group Anagrams
description: Given an array of lowercase strings, group the strings that are anagrams of each other and return the groups in any order. Constraints: 1 <= strs.length <= 10^4, 0 <= strs[i].length <= 100, and strs[i] consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Binary Tree Vertical Order Traversal
description: Given the root of a binary tree, return the vertical order traversal of its nodes' values: columns from left to right, and within each column nodes top-to-bottom. If two nodes share the same row and column, they should appear in left-to-right order. The tree has at most 100 nodes and node values are in [-100, 100].

title: Second Highest Salary
description: Given an Employee table with unique employee ids and their salaries, return the second highest DISTINCT salary. If a second distinct salary does not exist (e.g., only one unique salary), return null. The output must be a single row with the column name SecondHighestSalary.
optimal_strategy:
Select distinct salaries, sort them in descending order, and use LIMIT with OFFSET to fetch the second value, wrapping it in a scalar subquery so the result is a single row (null if missing).

```sql
SELECT
  (SELECT DISTINCT Salary
   FROM Employee
   ORDER BY Salary DESC
   LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1) AS SecondHighestSalary;
```

title: Special Binary String
description: Given a special binary string s (a binary string with equal numbers of 1's and 0's and every prefix having at least as many 1's as 0's), return the lexicographically largest string obtainable by swapping consecutive non-empty special substrings any number of times. The length of s is between 1 and 50 and s is guaranteed to be special.

title: Container With Most Water
description: Given an array height where the i-th element is the height of a vertical line at x = i, find two lines that together with the x-axis form a container that holds the maximum amount of water. The container's area is limited by the shorter line and the distance between the two indices; n can be up to 1e5 and heights up to 1e4.

title: Longest Common Prefix
description: Given an array of strings, return the longest common prefix shared by all strings. If no common prefix exists, return an empty string. Constraints: 1 <= strs.length <= 200 and each string length <= 200 (lowercase letters).

complexity.time: O(S) where S is the sum of all characters in the array (worst-case O(n * m))

title: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1)
description: Design a data structure that supports insert(val), remove(val), and getRandom(), each in average O(1) time. insert adds a value if not present and returns true/false, remove deletes if present and returns true/false, and getRandom returns a uniformly random element; up to 2e5 operations and 32-bit integer values.

complexity.time: Average: O(1) per operation (insert, remove, getRandom); worst-case O(n) for individual ops due to resizing

title: Nested List Weight Sum
description: Given a nested list where each element is either an integer or another nested list, compute the sum of every integer multiplied by its depth (number of enclosing lists). Depths start at 1 for top-level integers; nested depth can be up to 50 and total number of nested elements N is up to ~50 lists/elements per constraints.

title: Palindrome Number
description: Determine whether a given 32-bit signed integer x reads the same forward and backward (a palindrome). You must not convert the integer to a string; negative numbers and numbers ending in 0 (except 0 itself) are not palindromes.

complexity.time: O(log n) (specifically O(log_10 n) since we process digits)

title: Add Two Numbers
description: Given two non-empty linked lists representing non-negative integers with digits stored in reverse order, return a linked list representing their sum in the same reversed-digit format. Each node contains a single digit (0-9) and lists have length in [1, 100]; there are no leading zeros except for the number 0 itself.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
description: Given a string s, return the length of the longest substring that contains no repeating characters. The string length can be up to 5*10^4 and may contain letters, digits, symbols and spaces, so the solution should be linear or near-linear in practice.

title: Reordered Power of 2
description: Given an integer n (1 <= n <= 1e9), determine if its digits can be reordered (without leading zeros) to form a power of two. You may rearrange digits arbitrarily, but the resulting number must be an exact power of two. Return true if such a reordering exists, otherwise false.

title: Longest Palindromic Substring
description: Given a string s, return the longest substring of s that is a palindrome. The input length is between 1 and 1000 and s contains only digits and English letters.

title: Decode String
description: Given an encoded string where patterns of the form k[encoded_string] mean repeat encoded_string k times, return its fully decoded string. The input is guaranteed valid, contains only digits, lowercase letters and brackets, and decoded output length will not exceed 10^5.

complexity.time: O(maxK * n)  // (per editorial: n = length of input, maxK = largest repeat factor; repeats dominate work)
complexity.space: O(m + n)  // (per editorial: m = count of letters, n = count of digits / stack usage)

title: Roman to Integer
description: Convert a valid Roman numeral string (length 1..15, characters I,V,X,L,C,D,M) into its integer value by interpreting additive symbols and subtraction cases where a smaller symbol precedes a larger one.

title: Minimum Remove to Make Valid Parentheses
description: Given a string containing '(', ')' and lowercase letters, remove the minimum number of parentheses so the resulting string is a valid parentheses string (balanced and well-formed). The input length is up to 10^5, and any valid resulting string may be returned.

title: Simple Bank System
description: Simulate a simple bank with n accounts (numbered 1..n) that supports deposit, withdraw and transfer operations on integer balances. Each operation must validate account indices and sufficient funds before mutating balances; up to 10^4 calls per operation and balances/money up to 10^12.

complexity.time: transfer / deposit / withdraw: O(1) per call
complexity.space: O(n) to store balances (where n is the number of accounts)

title: Merge Intervals
description: Given a list of intervals [start, end], merge all overlapping intervals and return a list of non-overlapping intervals that covers all input intervals. Constraints: 1 <= intervals.length <= 10^4 and 0 <= start <= end <= 10^4, so an O(n log n) sort-based solution is acceptable.

complexity.space: O(log n) (or O(n) if sorting requires extra space / if you return a new array copy)

title: Random Pick with Weight
description: Given an array w of positive integer weights, implement pickIndex() to randomly return an index i with probability proportional to w[i] / sum(w). Constraints: 1 <= w.length <= 10^4, 1 <= w[i] <= 10^5, and pickIndex may be called up to 10^4 times.

example.output: 1  (index 1 is returned with probability 3/4, index 0 with probability 1/4)

complexity.time: Constructor: O(N); pickIndex: O(log N) per call
complexity.space: O(N) extra space for the prefix sums

title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree III
description: Given two distinct nodes p and q in a binary tree where each node has a parent pointer, return their lowest common ancestor (LCA). The tree can have up to 1e5 nodes, node values are unique, and both p and q are guaranteed to exist.

complexity.time: O(h) where h is the height of the tree (O(n) worst-case)

title: Create Hello World Function
description: Return a function factory createHelloWorld which produces a function that always returns the string "Hello World". The returned function should ignore any arguments passed to it (0 to 10 arguments per constraints).

title: Design Tic-Tac-Toe
description: Create a TicTacToe class to manage an n x n tic-tac-toe board that supports move(row, col, player) and returns 0 if no winner or the player id (1 or 2) when that move wins; moves are guaranteed valid, unique, and at most n^2 calls. n is between 2 and 100 and the game stops after a winning move.

complexity.space: O(n) (rows and cols arrays of length n, plus constant extra space)

title: Bitwise ORs of Subarrays
description: Given an integer array, return the number of distinct values obtainable by taking the bitwise OR of every non-empty contiguous subarray. The array length is up to 5*10^4 and elements are between 0 and 10^9, so an O(n * bits) solution is required rather than enumerating all O(n^2) subarrays.

complexity.time: O(n * B) where B is the number of bits in the values (B <= 31 for 10^9), effectively O(n)
complexity.space: O(U + B) where U is the number of distinct OR results (in worst case O(n * B)); additional O(B) for the per-index set

title: Valid Word Abbreviation
description: Given a word and an abbreviation, determine if the abbreviation correctly represents the word. The abbreviation may replace non-adjacent, non-empty substrings with their lengths (numbers with no leading zeros), and letters must match the original characters in order.

title: LRU Cache
description: Implement an LRU (least-recently-used) cache supporting get(key) and put(key, value) with O(1) average time per operation. The cache has a fixed positive capacity; when inserting a new item that would exceed capacity, evict the least recently used entry.

title: Vowel Spellchecker
description: Given a wordlist and a list of queries, implement a spellchecker that returns for each query either an exact case-sensitive match, the first case-insensitive match from the wordlist, the first match when all vowels are treated as wildcards (also case-insensitive), or the empty string if no match exists. Words and queries are short (length <= 7) and there are up to 5000 words/queries, so hash-based lookups are appropriate.

complexity.time: O(C) i.e. O((W + Q) * L) where W = |wordlist|, Q = |queries|, L = max word length
complexity.space: O(C) i.e. O(W * L) for the auxiliary maps/sets (plus output space)

title: 3Sum
description: Given an integer array nums, return all unique triplets [nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]] (i, j, k distinct) such that their sum is zero. Input length is 3..3000 and element values are in the range [-10^5, 10^5]; the result must not contain duplicate triplets.

complexity.space: O(log n) to O(n) (sorting overhead) excluding the output

title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
description: Given two sorted arrays, return the median of the combined sorted sequence. Arrays lengths m and n satisfy 1 <= m + n <= 2000 and the required overall runtime is O(log(m+n)).

title: Number of Islands
description: Given an m x n grid of '1's (land) and '0's (water), count how many connected islands exist where connectivity is horizontal/vertical only. Constraints: 1 <= m,n <= 300 and grid entries are '0' or '1'.

complexity.space: O(M * N) (worst-case stack/recursion when all cells are land)

title: Valid Word
description: Check whether a given string is a valid word: it must have length at least 3, contain only digits (0-9) and English letters (A-Z, a-z), and include at least one vowel and at least one consonant. Return true if all conditions hold, otherwise false.

title: Generate Parentheses
description: Generate all distinct well-formed parentheses strings using exactly n pairs. n ranges from 1 to 8, so the number of results is the nth Catalan number (grows exponentially), and recursion/backtracking depth is at most 2n.

title: Fruits Into Baskets III
description: Given two arrays fruits and baskets of length n, place each fruit type (in order) into the leftmost available basket whose capacity is >= that fruit's quantity, with each basket holding at most one fruit type; return how many fruit types remain unplaced. Key constraints: n up to 1e5 and values up to 1e9, so O(n^2) simulation is too slow.

title: Design Hit Counter
description: Design a hit counter that records hits at integer second timestamps and returns the number of hits in the past 5 minutes (300 seconds). Timestamps are provided in non-decreasing order and multiple hits can occur at the same timestamp.

complexity.time: hit: O(1); getHits: amortized O(1) (a single getHits can be O(n) to evict expired pairs, but each entry is removed at most once)
complexity.space: O(N) where N is the number of distinct timestamp entries stored (bounded in practice by hits within the last 300 seconds)

title: Count the Number of Infection Sequences
description: Given n people in a line and a sorted array sick of initially infected positions, count how many distinct orders the remaining people can become infected under the rule that at each step an uninfected person adjacent to any infected person becomes infected. Return the count modulo 1e9+7. Constraints: 2 <= n <= 1e5, sick.length in [1, n-1], sick is sorted.

title: Reaching Points
description: Given start point (sx, sy) and target (tx, ty), determine if you can reach the target by repeatedly replacing (x, y) with either (x+y, y) or (x, x+y). All coordinates are positive integers up to 1e9, so forward search is too large and a backwards (target-to-start) approach is required.

title: Trapping Rain Water II
description: Given an m x n grid of non-negative integers representing cell heights, compute how much water the 2D elevation map can trap after raining. Water can only be trapped if it is enclosed by higher boundaries and flows off the map edges; m and n are up to 200 and heights up to 2e4.

title: Text Justification
description: Given an array of words and a target maxWidth, pack words greedily into lines so each line has exactly maxWidth characters with spaces distributed evenly between words (left slots get extra spaces when necessary); the last line (or any line with a single word) must be left-justified. Each word length is > 0 and <= maxWidth, and there is at least one word.

complexity.time: O(n * k)  // n = number of words, k = average word length (or total characters)

title: Count Binary Substrings
description: Given a binary string s, count the number of non-empty substrings that contain an equal number of 0's and 1's and where all 0's and all 1's in each substring are grouped consecutively. The string length is up to 1e5 and contains only '0' and '1'.

title: IP to CIDR
description: Given a starting IPv4 address ip and a count n, produce the smallest list of CIDR blocks that exactly cover the inclusive range [ip, ip + n - 1] without covering addresses outside the range. The input ip is an IPv4 string and 1 <= n <= 1000, and every ip + x (x < n) stays within IPv4 space.

complexity.time: O(k) where k is the number of CIDR blocks produced (k <= 32, effectively O(log n) and bounded by 32)
complexity.space: O(k) extra space for the output list (excluding output), where k is the number of CIDR blocks

title: Meeting Rooms II
description: Given a list of meeting intervals [start, end], determine the minimum number of conference rooms needed so that no meetings that overlap share the same room. Meetings that start exactly when another ends do not overlap and can reuse the same room. You should return the smallest number of rooms that can accommodate all meetings.

title: Diagonal Traverse
description: Given an m x n matrix, return all elements in a zig-zag diagonal order (start at top-left and alternate directions for each diagonal). Constraints: 1 <= m, n and 1 <= m * n <= 10^4, so the total number of elements is at most 10^4.

complexity.space: O(1) extra (output array of size m * n not counted)

title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
description: Given an unsorted array of integers, return the length of the longest run of consecutive integers. The algorithm must run in O(n) time and nums length can be up to 1e5 with integer values in the range [-1e9, 1e9].

title: Shortest Distance from All Buildings
description: Given an m x n grid with 0 = empty land, 1 = building, and 2 = obstacle, find an empty cell to build a house such that the sum of shortest (4-directional) distances from that cell to all buildings is minimized. If no empty cell can reach all buildings (because of obstacles), return -1. Constraints: 1 <= m,n <= 50 and at least one building exists.

title: Reverse Integer
description: Given a signed 32-bit integer x, return x with its digits reversed. If the reversed value falls outside the signed 32-bit range [-2^31, 2^31 - 1], return 0; you cannot rely on 64-bit integer types.

complexity.time: O(log |x|) — proportional to the number of digits in x

title: Candy Crush
description: Given an m x n integer grid representing candies, repeatedly crush any group of three or more identical candies adjacent horizontally or vertically (setting them to 0), then let candies fall down to fill empty spaces, and repeat until no more candies can be crushed; return the final stable board. Constraints: 3 <= m, n <= 50 and candy values are positive integers (0 represents empty).

complexity.time: O(m^2 * n^2) (worst-case; O(m*n) per iteration times up to O(m*n) iterations)

title: Maximum Subarray
description: Given an integer array nums, return the largest sum of any contiguous subarray. The array length is up to 10^5 and elements range from -10^4 to 10^4, so an O(n) time and O(1) space solution is expected; the problem also suggests a divide-and-conquer follow-up.

title: Pascal's Triangle
description: Generate the first numRows of Pascal's triangle where each row starts and ends with 1 and each interior value is the sum of the two numbers above it. numRows is between 1 and 30, so a simple iterative construction is efficient and fits easily in memory.

complexity.space: O(1) (excluding the output, which requires O(numRows^2) space)

title: Delete Duplicate Folders in System
description: Given a list of absolute folder paths, remove all folders that have duplicate subtree structure (i.e., the same non-empty set of named subfolders and identical nested structure) occurring two or more times; when a folder is marked as duplicate its entire subtree is deleted. Return the remaining folder paths in any order. Constraints: up to 2*10^4 paths, total characters across all names <= 2*10^5, folder names are lowercase and ≤10 chars.

complexity.time: O(S log C) where S is the total number of characters across all folder names in input (≤ 2e5) and the log factor comes from sorting child serializations per node.
complexity.space: O(S) to store the trie, serializations, and hash map of serialization counts (proportional to total serialized string length).

title: Maximum Score From Removing Substrings
description: Given a string s and two integers x and y, you can repeatedly remove substrings "ab" for x points or "ba" for y points; return the maximum points obtainable. The string length is up to 1e5 and x,y up to 1e4, so an O(n) greedy solution is required.

title: Maximum Number of Distinct Elements After Operations
description: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, you may add any integer in [-k, k] to each element at most once; return the maximum number of distinct elements possible after doing these operations. Constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 1e5, 1 <= nums[i] <= 1e9, 0 <= k <= 1e9.

complexity.space: O(log n) (in-place sort; O(n) worst-case depending on language/sort implementation)

title: Next Permutation
description: Rearrange the given array of integers into the lexicographically next greater permutation; if no such permutation exists, rearrange into the lowest possible order (ascending). The change must be done in-place using only constant extra memory (1 <= nums.length <= 100, 0 <= nums[i] <= 100).

title: Maximum Unique Subarray Sum After Deletion
description: Given an integer array nums, you may delete any number of elements (but not all) and then choose a contiguous subarray whose elements are all unique; the task is to maximize the sum of that chosen subarray. Constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 100 and -100 <= nums[i] <= 100.

title: Rearranging Fruits
description: Given two arrays basket1 and basket2 of length n with fruit costs, determine the minimum total cost to make the multisets equal by swapping items between baskets where swapping basket1[i] with basket2[j] costs min(basket1[i], basket2[j]); return -1 if impossible. Key constraints: n up to 1e5 and values up to 1e9, so linear or n log n solutions with O(n) extra memory are expected.

title: Spiral Matrix
description: Given an m x n integer matrix, return all its elements in spiral order (starting from the top-left, moving right, then down, then left, then up, repeating until all elements are visited). Constraints: 1 <= m, n <= 10 and matrix values are between -100 and 100.

title: All O`one Data Structure
description: Maintain counts for string keys with O(1) average-time updates and queries; support incrementing and decrementing a key (removing when count reaches 0) and returning any key with the current minimum or maximum count. Keys are short lowercase strings and there are up to 5e4 operations, so the structure must be efficient in time and linear in the number of unique keys.

complexity.space: O(N) where N is the number of unique keys stored

title: Find the Celebrity
description: Given n people labeled 0..n-1 and an API knows(a,b) that returns whether person a knows person b, determine if there is a celebrity (everyone else knows them, and they know nobody). You may only use the knows API and should minimize calls; n is between 2 and 100 and graph[i][i] == 1.

title: Valid Palindrome II
description: Given a string s, determine whether it can become a palindrome after deleting at most one character. The string length is up to 10^5 and contains lowercase English letters, so the solution should be linear or near-linear time and constant extra space.

title: Number of Black Blocks
description: Given an m x n grid with some cells colored black (others white), count how many 2x2 blocks contain exactly 0,1,2,3,4 black cells and return an array arr of length 5 with those counts. Constraints: 2 <= m,n <= 1e5 and coordinates.length <= 1e4 (all coordinates distinct).

complexity.time: O(k) where k = coordinates.length (each black cell updates up to 4 blocks, constant work per update)
complexity.space: O(k) extra space for the map (only blocks that have >=1 black cell are stored)

title: Minimum Operations to Write the Letter Y on a Grid
description: Given an odd n x n grid with values 0, 1, or 2, mark the cells that form a letter Y (two diagonals from the top corners to the center and a vertical line from the center to the bottom). You may change any cell value to 0/1/2 in one operation; return the minimum operations required so that all Y-cells share one value and all non-Y-cells share a different value.

title: Analyze User Website Visit Pattern
description: Given parallel arrays username, timestamp, and website describing visits, return the 3-website pattern visited (not necessarily contiguously) by the largest number of distinct users; ties are broken by lexicographic order. Arrays length n is up to 50 and timestamps are unique so you should sort by time, group visits per user, and count unique 3-sequences per user.

complexity.time: O(n log n + sum_u m_u^3) -> worst-case O(n^3) (sorting O(n log n) plus generating all 3-sequences per user; worst when one user has O(n) visits).
complexity.space: O(n^3) worst-case for storing all unique patterns (practically O(n + number_of_patterns)), with O(n) for records and per-user lists.

title: Maximum Erasure Value
description: Given an array of positive integers, find the maximum sum of any contiguous subarray that contains only unique elements. You must choose exactly one such subarray; array length is up to 1e5 and values are up to 1e4.

complexity.space: O(n) (worst-case, when all elements are unique)

title: Add Two Integers
description: Given two integers num1 and num2, return their sum. Each input is constrained to the range [-100, 100], so overflow is not a concern in typical integer types.

title: Collect Coins in a Tree
description: Given an unrooted tree with n nodes and some nodes containing coins (coins[i] is 0 or 1), you may start at any vertex and repeatedly either collect all coins within distance 2 of your current vertex or move along an edge to an adjacent vertex. Return the minimum number of edge traversals required to collect all coins and return to the starting vertex (counting repeated traversals).

title: 24 Game
description: Given 4 cards with values in [1,9], determine whether you can insert the operators +, -, *, / and parentheses to form an expression that evaluates to 24 (division is real division). You may only perform binary operations (no unary -) and cannot concatenate digits; the order of using numbers is arbitrary.

complexity.time: O(N^3 * 3^{N-1} * N! * (N-1)!) (as given in the editorial; for the problem N=4 this is constant-time in practice)

title: Fruits Into Baskets II
description: Given two arrays fruits and baskets of equal length n, place each fruit type (in left-to-right order) into the leftmost available basket whose capacity is >= that fruit's quantity, where each basket can be used at most once. If a fruit cannot be placed in any basket, it remains unplaced; return the count of such unplaced fruit types. Constraints: 1 <= n <= 100 and 1 <= fruits[i], baskets[i] <= 1000.

title: Merge Sorted Array
description: Given two sorted integer arrays nums1 and nums2 and counts m and n of valid elements in each, merge nums2 into nums1 in non-decreasing order in-place (nums1 has length m + n with trailing zeros to hold nums2). The function should modify nums1 directly and not return anything; constraints: 0 <= m,n <= 200 and values fit in 32-bit signed range.

title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
description: Return the k-th largest element in an integer array (k is 1-indexed); input size can be up to 1e5 and elements range from -1e4 to 1e4. The problem asks for the k-th largest value in sorted order (not necessarily distinct) and requests a solution that avoids full sorting if possible.

title: Brightest Position on Street
description: Given lamps specified by (position, range) that light the inclusive interval [position-range, position+range], find the integer position with the maximum number of lamps covering it, breaking ties by the smallest position. Constraints: up to 1e5 lamps and positions/ranges up to +/-1e8, so an O(n log n) solution is appropriate.

title: Basic Calculator II
description: Evaluate a mathematical expression string containing non-negative integers and the operators +, -, *, / (with spaces allowed). The expression has no parentheses and integer division must truncate toward zero; input length can be up to 3*10^5.

title: Minimum Operations to Reduce an Integer to 0
description: Given a positive integer n, you may add or subtract any power of two (2^i) any number of times; return the minimum number of such operations required to reach 0. Constraint: 1 <= n <= 10^5, so an O(log n) bitwise solution is expected.

title: Find the Length of the Longest Common Prefix
description: Given two arrays of positive integers arr1 and arr2, find the length (number of digits) of the longest integer that is a prefix of some number in arr1 and also a prefix of some number in arr2. Prefixes are formed by taking leading digits (e.g., 123 is a prefix of 12345). Array sizes can be up to 5e4 and values up to 1e8, so digit-based reductions (dividing by 10) are efficient.

complexity.time: O(m * log10 M + n * log10 N) where m = |arr1|, n = |arr2|, M and N are the max values in arr1 and arr2 (digits = log10(value))
complexity.space: O(m * log10 M) to store all prefixes from arr1

title: Number of Ways to Wear Different Hats to Each Other
description: Given n (<=10) people and 40 possible hat types (1..40), each person has a list of preferred hats. Count the number of ways to assign distinct hats so every person gets exactly one preferred hat, returning the answer modulo 10^9+7.

complexity.time: O(k * n * 2^n) where k = 40 (so effectively O(n * 2^n))
complexity.space: O(k * 2^n) (for memoization), plus O(k + n) for auxiliary structures

title: Koko Eating Bananas
description: Given n piles of bananas and h hours, choose the minimum integer eating speed k (bananas/hour) such that Koko can finish all piles within h hours; eating k bananas from a chosen pile takes 1 hour (if fewer than k remain she finishes that pile and wastes the rest of the hour). Key constraints: 1 <= piles.length <= 10^4, piles[i] and h up to 10^9, and h >= piles.length.

complexity.time: O(n * log m) where n = piles.length and m = max(piles)

title: Climbing Stairs
description: You need to count how many distinct ways to climb to the top of a staircase with n steps when each move is either 1 or 2 steps. Constraints: 1 <= n <= 45, so the answer fits comfortably in a 32-bit integer.

title: Buildings With an Ocean View
description: Given an array heights of n building heights in a line with the ocean to the right, return the indices of buildings that can see the ocean (i.e., every building to their right is strictly shorter). n is up to 1e5 and heights[i] up to 1e9, so an O(n) solution is required.

complexity.space: O(1) extra (O(n) if you count the output list)

title: Integer to English Words
description: Convert a non-negative integer into its English words representation, using correct scale words (Thousand, Million, Billion) and capitalization; input ranges from 0 to 2,147,483,647 and output should have single spaces and no trailing spaces. The solution must correctly handle special names for numbers < 20 and compose larger numbers by grouping digits.

example.output: One Million Two Hundred Thirty Four Thousand Five Hundred Sixty Seven

title: Number of People Aware of a Secret
description: Starting with one person knowing a secret on day 1, each person begins sharing the secret every day after delay days and forgets it after forget days (they cannot share on or after the forget day). Given n, return how many people know the secret at the end of day n, modulo 10^9+7. Constraints: 2 <= n <= 1000 and 1 <= delay < forget <= n.

title: Invalid Transactions
description: Given a list of transactions formatted as "name,time,amount,city", return all transactions that are possibly invalid: amount > 1000 or there exists another transaction with the same name in a different city within a 60-minute window. There are at most 1000 transactions and times/amounts are small integers.

complexity.time: O(n log n) for sorting groups, but O(n^2) in the worst case across name-groups due to pairwise checks (overall worst-case O(n^2)), where n = number of transactions
complexity.space: O(n) auxiliary space for parsed transactions and bookkeeping

title: Maximum Average Pass Ratio
description: Given classes[i] = [pass_i, total_i] and extraStudents brilliant students (each guaranteed to pass in the class they are assigned), assign the extra students to maximize the average of pass_i/total_i across all classes. Constraints: up to 1e5 classes and up to 1e5 extra students, with pass_i <= total_i <= 1e5.

complexity.time: O(k * log n + n) where n = number of classes and k = extraStudents

title: Avoid Flood in The City
description: You are given a sequence of days; rains[i] > 0 means lake rains[i] gets full that day (and causes a flood if it was already full), and rains[i] == 0 means a sunny day on which you may choose one lake to dry. Return an array where rainy days are -1 and sunny days specify which lake to dry so that no lake ever floods, or return [] if impossible. Constraints: up to 1e5 days and lake ids up to 1e9.

complexity.time: O(n log n) (uses an ordered set / binary search for sunny days; languages with a balanced tree give O(n log n) overall)
complexity.space: O(n) (for answer array, last-rain map, and the set/list of sunny days)

title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
description: Merge two sorted singly-linked lists by splicing together their nodes to produce one sorted list and return its head. Both input lists are sorted in non-decreasing order, contain between 0 and 50 nodes each, and node values lie in [-100, 100].

title: LFU Cache
description: Implement an LFU (Least Frequently Used) cache that supports get(key) and put(key, value) in average O(1) time. When capacity is exceeded, evict the key with the smallest access frequency, and break ties by evicting the least recently used key among those with the same frequency.

complexity.space: O(capacity) (stores up to capacity nodes and supporting maps/lists)

title: Smallest Missing Non-negative Integer After Operations
description: Given an integer array nums and an integer value k, you may add or subtract k any number of times to any element. Return the maximum possible MEX (minimum excluded non-negative integer) of nums after applying these operations; 1 <= nums.length, value <= 10^5 and nums[i] can be negative or large in magnitude.

title: N-Queens
description: Place n queens on an n x n chessboard so that no two queens attack each other (no shared row, column, or diagonal). Return all distinct board configurations; n is between 1 and 9, so exponential-time backtracking is acceptable.

title: Minimum Number of Increments on Subarrays to Form a Target Array
description: Given a target array and an initially all-zero array of the same length, you may increment every element of any chosen contiguous subarray by 1 in a single operation. The task is to find the minimum number of such operations required to transform the initial array into target. Constraints: 1 <= target.length <= 1e5, 1 <= target[i] <= 1e5, and the answer fits in a 32-bit integer.

title: Range Product Queries of Powers
description: Write n as the multiset of powers of two corresponding to its set bits (smallest number of powers), then for each query [l,r] return the product of powers[l..r] modulo 1e9+7. Constraints: 1 <= n <= 1e9 so there are at most ~30 elements in the powers array, and up to 1e5 queries.

complexity.time: O(log n + q * log M) where M = 1e9+7 (practically O(log n + q) since exponents are small)

title: Find Peak Element
description: Given an integer array nums where nums[i] != nums[i+1], find and return the index of any peak element (an element strictly greater than its neighbors). You may assume virtual neighbors nums[-1] and nums[n] are -∞. The algorithm must run in O(log n) time and nums.length >= 1.

title: Design In-Memory File System
description: Simulate an in-memory hierarchical file system supporting ls, mkdir, addContentToFile, and readContentFromFile. Paths are absolute, use '/' as separator, directories and files are distinct, and ls must return names in lexicographic order.

complexity.time: Per operation: ls O(m + n + k log k) (m = path string length to split, n = path depth, k = entries in directory); mkdir O(m + n); addContentToFile and readContentFromFile O(m + n).
complexity.space: O(N + S) where N is the total number of directory/file nodes (path components) stored and S is the total length of all file contents.

title: Find the Minimum Area to Cover All Ones II
description: Given a binary 2D grid, place three non-overlapping axis-aligned rectangles (they may touch) so that every '1' lies inside at least one rectangle and the total area of the three rectangles is minimized. Grid dimensions are up to 30x30 and there are at least three '1's in the grid.

title: Rotate Image
description: Given an n x n matrix, rotate it 90 degrees clockwise in-place (modify the input matrix without allocating another 2D matrix). Constraints: n == matrix.length == matrix[i].length, 1 <= n <= 20, and elements are integers in [-1000, 1000].

title: Find the Number of Ways to Place People I
description: Given n distinct integer points on a 2D plane, count ordered pairs (A, B) such that A is on the upper-left side of B (i.e., A.x <= B.x and A.y >= B.y) and the axis-aligned rectangle (including its border) with corners A and B contains no other points. Constraints: 2 <= n <= 50 and coordinates are in [0,50].

complexity.time: O(n^2) (sorting O(n log n) + scan O(n^2), dominated by O(n^2))
complexity.space: O(1) auxiliary (plus O(n) for the sorted copy / language-dependent sort auxiliary space)

title: Dot Product of Two Sparse Vectors
description: Given two vectors that are mostly zeros, implement a SparseVector class that stores a vector efficiently and computes the dot product with another SparseVector. Key constraints: vector length n up to 1e5 and values are non-negative integers; you should avoid iterating the full length when many entries are zero.

complexity.time: Constructor: O(n) to scan the input; dotProduct: O(L1 + L2) where L1 and L2 are counts of non-zero entries in the two vectors.
complexity.space: O(L) extra space to store non-zero entries (L = number of non-zero elements in the stored vector).

title: Fizz Buzz
description: Given an integer n, return a 1-indexed string array of length n where each position i contains "Fizz" if i is divisible by 3, "Buzz" if i is divisible by 5, "FizzBuzz" if divisible by both, or the number i as a string otherwise. Constraints: 1 <= n <= 10^4, so a simple linear pass is sufficient.

complexity.space: O(1) extra space (O(n) total including the output array)

title: Smallest Subarrays With Maximum Bitwise OR
description: Given an array nums, for each index i find the length of the shortest non-empty subarray starting at i whose bitwise OR equals the maximum OR obtainable by any subarray starting at i. n up to 1e5 and nums[i] up to 1e9 (so at most ~31 bits).

complexity.time: O(n * log C) where log C ≈ 31 (so effectively O(n))
complexity.space: O(log C) (≈ O(31), i.e., O(1) auxiliary space)

title: Valid Triangle Number
description: Given an integer array nums, count how many triplets (i, j, k) can form the side lengths of a triangle (i.e., satisfy the triangle inequality). Constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 1000 and 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000, so an O(n^2) algorithm is expected for interviews rather than brute force.

complexity.space: O(log n) (sorting stack) or O(1) extra

title: Simplify Path
description: Given an absolute Unix-style path, return its simplified canonical path by resolving '.' (current dir), '..' (parent dir), and collapsing multiple slashes. The input always starts with '/' and has length up to 3000, containing letters, digits, '.', '/', and '_'.

complexity.time: O(N) time, where N = path.length (split + single pass over components)
complexity.space: O(N) extra space for the split components and the stack

title: Number of Ships in a Rectangle
description: Given an interactive API Sea.hasShips(topRight, bottomLeft) that tells whether at least one ship exists inside an axis-aligned integer rectangle, count how many ships lie inside a given rectangle. Coordinates are integers in [0,1000], topRight != bottomLeft, and there are at most 10 ships in the query rectangle; you may call hasShips at most 400 times.

complexity.time: O(S * (log2(max(M, N)) - log4 S)) where M,N are side-lengths of the rectangle and S (<=10) is the number of ships (often summarized as O(S * log max(M, N))).
complexity.space: O(log2(max(M, N))) due to recursion stack

title: Making A Large Island
description: Given an n x n binary grid where 1 = land and 0 = water, you may flip at most one 0 to 1; return the size of the largest 4-directionally connected island possible after the flip. n is up to 500, so an O(n^2) solution (or O(grid cells)) is required.

title: Minimum Score After Removals on a Tree
description: Given a tree with n nodes (values in nums) remove two distinct edges to form three connected components and compute the XOR of node values in each component; return the minimum possible difference between the largest and smallest of those three XOR values. Constraints: 3 <= n <= 1000, nums[i] up to 1e8, edges form a valid tree.

title: Maximum Profit in Job Scheduling
description: Given arrays startTime, endTime and profit for n jobs, choose a subset of non-overlapping jobs (jobs can touch: start == end allowed) to maximize total profit. n is up to 5e4 and times can be large, so an O(N log N) solution is required.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
description: Given a distinct-integer array nums that was sorted in ascending order and then possibly rotated, return the index of target in nums or -1 if not present; the solution must run in O(log n) time. Constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 5000 and all values are unique.

title: Find the Maximum Length of Valid Subsequence I
description: Given an integer array nums, find the length of the longest subsequence whose consecutive pair sums all have the same parity. The array length can be up to 2*10^5 and values up to 10^7, so an O(n) solution with O(1) extra space is required.

title: Merge k Sorted Lists
description: Given an array of k sorted linked lists, merge them into a single sorted linked list and return its head. Lists may be empty; total number of nodes across all lists is N and k can be up to 10^4, so an algorithm that scales with N and k is required.

complexity.space: O(k) (extra space for the heap; result reuses existing nodes so no O(N) extra required)

title: Majority Element
description: Given an array nums of length n, return the majority element — the value that appears more than floor(n/2) times. You may assume a majority element always exists; n ranges up to 5*10^4 and nums[i] fits in 32-bit signed integer.

title: Design Task Manager
description: Manage tasks across users supporting add, edit, remove, and execute-top operations where execute returns and removes the task with highest priority (tie-break by larger taskId). Up to 2e5 operations and initial tasks up to 1e5 require efficient (logarithmic) retrieval and lazy deletion of stale entries.

complexity.time: Initialization: O(n log n). add/edit: O(log(n+m)). rmv: O(1). execTop: amortized O(log(n+m)).
complexity.space: O(n + m) (map + heap may contain many stale entries from edits/adds)

title: Recyclable and Low Fat Products
description: Given a Products table where each row has product_id and two ENUM columns low_fats and recyclable (each 'Y' or 'N'), return the product_id values for products that are both low fat and recyclable. The table can be returned in any order; product_id is unique.

example.input:
products = [
  { product_id: 0, low_fats: 'Y', recyclable: 'N' },
  { product_id: 1, low_fats: 'Y', recyclable: 'Y' },
  { product_id: 2, low_fats: 'N', recyclable: 'Y' },
  { product_id: 3, low_fats: 'Y', recyclable: 'Y' },
  { product_id: 4, low_fats: 'N', recyclable: 'N' }
]

complexity.space: O(n) (O(1) auxiliary, O(n) to store the output in the worst case)

title: Minimum Edge Reversals So Every Node Is Reachable
description: Given a directed tree-like graph of n nodes (0..n-1) with n-1 directed edges, compute for every node i the minimum number of edge reversals required so that starting from i you can reach every other node via directed edges. Constraints: n up to 1e5 and edges form a tree when treated as undirected (edges.length == n-1).

title: Coin Change
description: Given coin denominations and a target amount, return the minimum number of coins needed to make that amount using an unlimited supply of each coin, or -1 if it's impossible. Constraints: up to 12 coin types, coin values up to 2^31-1, and amount up to 10^4.

title: Allocate Mailboxes
description: Given positions of houses on a street and an integer k, place k mailboxes to minimize the sum of distances from each house to its nearest mailbox. Houses are unique, n = houses.length is at most 100, and mailbox positions can be any integer (optimal is at medians of segments).

title: Remove Sub-Folders from the Filesystem
description: Given a list of absolute folder paths, return the list after removing any folder that is a sub-folder of another (a path X is a sub-folder of Y if X starts with Y followed by '/'). Constraints: 1 <= folder.length <= 4*10^4, each path length up to 100, and all folder names are unique.

complexity.time: O(N * L * log N)  (N = number of folders, L = max path length)
complexity.space: O(N * L)  (result + sorting overhead / storage of paths)

title: Combine Two Tables
description: Given two tables, Person (personId, lastName, firstName) and Address (addressId, personId, city, state), return each person's first name, last name, city and state; if a person has no address row, city and state should be null. The result can be returned in any order and personId is the join key (Person is the left table).

example.input: Person = [{ personId: 1, lastName: 'Wang', firstName: 'Allen' }, { personId: 2, lastName: 'Alice', firstName: 'Bob' }], Address = [{ addressId: 1, personId: 2, city: 'New York City', state: 'New York' }, { addressId: 2, personId: 3, city: 'Leetcode', state: 'California' }]
example.output: [{ firstName: 'Allen', lastName: 'Wang', city: null, state: null }, { firstName: 'Bob', lastName: 'Alice', city: 'New York City', state: 'New York' }]

complexity.time: O(P + A) where P = number of Person rows and A = number of Address rows
complexity.space: O(A) extra space for the address map (or O(P + A) if you count the output array)

title: Maximum Fruits Harvested After at Most K Steps
description: You start at startPos on an infinite x-axis and can walk at most k total steps; fruits[i] = [positioni, amounti] gives how many fruits are at that position (positions sorted). Return the maximum fruits you can collect by visiting positions (each position's fruits are picked once) within the step limit k.

title: String Compression
description: Given an array of characters, compress it in-place by replacing each consecutive group of the same character with the character followed by the group's length (omit the length if it is 1), and return the new length. The algorithm must use only constant extra space and the characters beyond the returned length can be ignored. Input length is between 1 and 2000 and chars contain printable characters.

example.output: Return 6, and the first 6 characters are ["a","2","b","2","c","3"]

title: Find N Unique Integers Sum up to Zero
description: Given an integer n (1 <= n <= 1000), return any array of n distinct integers whose sum is zero. The array may contain any integers as long as they are unique and sum to 0.

complexity.space: O(1) extra (O(n) including the output array)

title: Water Bottles
description: You start with numBottles full water bottles and can trade numExchange empty bottles for one full bottle. Repeatedly drink and exchange until you can no longer make an exchange; return the total number of bottles you can drink. Constraints: 1 <= numBottles <= 100 and 2 <= numExchange <= 100.

title: Minimum Difference in Sums After Removal of Elements
description: Given an array nums of length 3n, remove exactly n elements (a subsequence) so the remaining 2n elements split into a first n and second n block; return the minimum possible value of sum(first) - sum(second) after removal. Key constraints: nums.length = 3n with 1 <= n <= 1e5 and values up to 1e5, so an O(n log n) solution with O(n) extra space is required.

title: Minimum Time to Complete All Deliveries
description: Two drones must complete d1 and d2 one-hour deliveries each. Each drone i is unavailable at hours that are multiples of ri (recharge) and only one delivery can occur per hour; find the minimum total hours T so both drones can finish all deliveries.

complexity.time: O(log Answer) where Answer is the returned minimum time (each feasibility check is O(1))

title: Find the Closest Palindrome
description: Given a string n representing a positive integer (no leading zeros) of length up to 18, return the closest integer (as a string) that is a palindrome and not equal to n itself. If two palindromes are equally close, return the smaller one; distance is measured by absolute difference.

title: Optimal Account Balancing
description: Compute each persons net balance from the transactions and return the minimum number of transfers required to settle all debts. Key constraints: up to 8 transactions and up to 12 distinct person IDs; only people with non-zero net balance matter (their count m is small).

complexity.time: O((n - 1)!) where n is the number of non-zero balances (worst-case backtracking)
complexity.space: O(n) (balances array + recursion stack, where n is the number of non-zero balances)

title: Next Greater Numerically Balanced Number
description: Given an integer n (0 <= n <= 10^6), return the smallest numerically balanced number strictly greater than n. A number is numerically balanced if for every digit d that appears in the number, the digit appears exactly d times (digits '0' may not appear).

complexity.time: O(log C) per query after precomputation (precompute scans up to constant MAX), where C is the count of balanced numbers

title: Minimum Operations to Make the Integer Zero
description: Given num1 and num2, you may perform operations where in each operation you pick i in [0,60] and subtract (2^i + num2) from num1; return the minimum number of operations required to make num1 equal to 0, or -1 if impossible. Key observations: if you perform k operations, x = num1 - k * num2 must be expressible as the sum of k powers of two, which is equivalent to requiring popcount(x) <= k <= x. Constraints: 1 <= num1 <= 1e9, -1e9 <= num2 <= 1e9.

complexity.time: O(log num1) (equivalently O(60 * log X) bounded by constant 60 iterations, each counting bits of x)

title: Alien Dictionary
description: Given a list of words sorted according to an unknown order of lowercase English letters, determine a possible ordering of the letters that is consistent with the list. If no valid ordering exists (e.g., due to a cycle or a word appearing before its own prefix), return an empty string. Constraints: 1 <= words.length <= 100, each word length <= 100, letters are lowercase.

complexity.time: O(C) where C is the total number of characters across all words (building relations + topological sort)
complexity.space: O(U + min(U^2, N)) where U is the number of unique letters and N is number of words (adjacency + indegree), which is O(1) for U ≤ 26 but generalized as above

title: Maximum Running Time of N Computers
description: Given n computers and an array batteries where batteries[i] is minutes that battery can run a computer, determine the maximum number of minutes all n computers can run simultaneously if you may swap batteries between computers at integer times (no recharging). Constraints: 1 <= n <= batteries.length <= 1e5 and 1 <= batteries[i] <= 1e9.

complexity.time: O(m * log k) where m = batteries.length and k = max possible running time (≈ sum(batteries)/n)

title: Word Search
description: Given an m x n grid of characters and a target word, determine if the word can be formed by sequentially adjacent cells (horizontal or vertical) without reusing any cell. Constraints: 1 <= m,n <= 6 and 1 <= word.length <= 15, so a DFS/backtracking search from each cell is feasible.

complexity.time: O(N * 3^L) where N = m * n and L = word.length

title: Reorganize String
description: Rearrange the letters of a given string so that no two adjacent characters are the same, or return an empty string if no such arrangement exists. The string length is between 1 and 500 and contains only lowercase English letters; if any character appears more than ceil(n/2) times, a valid rearrangement is impossible.

complexity.time: O(N log k) (N = length of string, k = number of unique chars; since k ≤ 26 this is effectively O(N))
complexity.space: O(k) (only frequency map and heap of size ≤ k, with k ≤ 26 so effectively O(1))

title: Find X-Sum of All K-Long Subarrays I
description: Given an integer array nums and integers k and x, compute for every contiguous subarray of length k the x-sum: keep only the top x most frequent elements (breaking ties by larger element) and sum their occurrences multiplied by the element values. Constraints are small (n <= 50, nums[i] <= 50) and 1 <= x <= k <= n.

title: Robot Room Cleaner
description: Control a blindfolded robot placed on an unknown empty cell in an m x n grid (0 = wall, 1 = empty) using only move/turn/clean APIs, and clean every reachable empty cell. You do not know the room layout or starting coordinates; the robot initially faces up and the room edges are walls, with at most 100x200 grid size and all empty cells reachable from the start.

complexity.time: O(number_of_accessible_cells) which equals O(N - M) where N is total cells and M is obstacles (each accessible cell checked in 4 directions => ~4*(N-M) operations)
complexity.space: O(number_of_accessible_cells) = O(N - M) due to visited set and recursion stack

title: Line Reflection
description: Given n points on a 2D plane, determine whether there exists a vertical line (x = c) such that reflecting all points across that line yields the same multiset of points. Points may repeat and coordinates are integers in range [-1e8, 1e8], with n up to 1e4.

title: Lexicographically Smallest Generated String
description: Given two strings str1 (length n, composed of 'T'/'F') and str2 (length m), construct a string word of length n + m - 1 using lowercase letters such that for each i: if str1[i]=='T' then word[i..i+m-1]==str2, and if str1[i]=='F' then word[i..i+m-1]!=str2. Return the lexicographically smallest such word or "" if impossible. Constraints: n up to 10^4, m up to 500.

title: Maximum Frequency of an Element After Performing Operations I
description: Given an integer array nums and two integers k and numOperations, you may choose up to numOperations distinct indices and add any value in [-k, k] to each chosen element; return the maximum possible frequency (count of equal values) of any element after operations. Constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 1e5, 0 <= k <= 1e5, and 0 <= numOperations <= nums.length, so solutions should be near linear or n log n in practice.

complexity.time: O(n log n + R log n) where n = nums.length and R = max(nums) - min(nums) (the range of enumerated target values); equivalently O(max(n log n, R log n)).
complexity.space: O(n) (for the sorted array copy and frequency map)

title: Largest Number
description: Given a list of non-negative integers, arrange them so that their concatenation yields the largest possible number and return that number as a string; numbers can be up to 10^9 and the list length is up to 100. Treat numbers as strings for ordering, and handle the all-zero edge case by returning "0".

complexity.time: O(n log n) (sorting; comparisons cost up to the average string length, so O(n log n * m) if m is avg digits)

title: Sliding Window Maximum
description: Given an integer array nums and a window size k, slide the window from left to right and return the maximum value in each window. Constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 10^5, -10^4 <= nums[i] <= 10^4, and 1 <= k <= nums.length.

title: Soup Servings
description: You have two soups A and B each with n mL and repeatedly apply one of four equiprobable serving operations (100/0, 75/25, 50/50, 25/75) until one or both soups are empty; return P(A empties first) + 0.5 * P(both empty same turn). Because all servings are multiples of 25 mL, convert n to m = ceil(n/25) servings and work on integer-serving DP. n can be up to 1e9 so use the observation that for sufficiently large m the answer ≈ 1 and can be returned early to meet the 1e-5 tolerance.

complexity.time: O(min(m, m0)^2) where m = ceil(n/25) and m0 ≈ 200 (so practically O(1) for the 1e-5 tolerance)
complexity.space: O(min(m, m0)^2) (memo table), which is O(1) in practice given m0 ≈ 200

title: Find the Minimum Amount of Time to Brew Potions
description: Given n wizards and m potions, each potion j must be processed by all wizards in order, where wizard i takes skill[i] * mana[j] time on potion j. Wizards can work on at most one potion at a time and a potion must be passed immediately to the next wizard upon completion; return the minimum time to finish all m potions. Constraints: 1 <= n, m <= 5000 and 1 <= skill[i], mana[j] <= 5000.

title: Make Array Elements Equal to Zero
description: Given an integer array nums, pick a starting index curr where nums[curr]==0 and an initial direction (left or right). A pointer moves stepwise: if it lands on 0 it continues same direction; if it lands on a positive value it decrements that value by 1, reverses direction, and steps; the selection is valid if after the process every element becomes 0. n = nums.length is up to 100 and nums[i] up to 100, and at least one zero exists.

title: Top K Frequent Elements
description: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the k most frequent elements from the array (any order). Constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 1e5, element values in [-1e4, 1e4], and 1 <= k <= number of unique elements (answer is guaranteed unique).

title: Minimum Number of People to Teach
description: Given n languages, m users (languages.length == m) and a list of friendship pairs, choose one language to teach to some users so that every friendship pair shares at least one common language. Return the minimum number of users to teach. Constraints: n, m, and friendships.length are ≤ 500, and languages[i] contains unique language ids in [1..n].

complexity.time: O(m * n) (where m is number of friendships and n is number of languages)
complexity.space: O(m + n) (space for the set of bad users and the per-language counts; plus small per-user sets)

title: Max Stack
description: Implement a stack that supports standard stack operations plus retrieving and removing the maximum element. The data structure must support top in O(1) and other operations in O(log n) (amortized where applicable); up to 1e5 operations and values in range [-1e7,1e7].

complexity.time: push: O(log n), pop: O(log n) amortized, popMax: O(log n) amortized, top: O(1) amortized, peekMax: O(1) amortized

title: Find the Maximum Number of Fruits Collected
description: Three children start at corners (0,0), (0,n-1) and (n-1,0) of an n x n grid and must each make exactly n-1 moves to reach (n-1,n-1); when a child enters a room they collect all fruits there and if multiple children enter the same room the fruits are collected only once. Because the child from (0,0) is forced to follow the main diagonal, we can compute its diagonal contribution and then use dynamic programming (with a rolling 1D array) to compute the best collection for each of the other two children restricted to one side of the diagonal, reusing the same DP on a transposed matrix for the symmetric side.

title: Minimum Absolute Difference Between Elements With Constraint
description: Given an array nums and an integer x, find the minimum absolute difference |nums[i] - nums[j]| among pairs of indices i, j that satisfy |i - j| >= x. n = nums.length can be up to 1e5 and values up to 1e9, so an O(n log n) approach is desirable.

title: Bus Routes
description: Given a list of bus routes (each route is a cycle of stops), return the minimum number of buses required to go from source stop to target stop using only buses, or -1 if impossible. You start off-bus at source; constraints: up to M=500 routes, sum of all route lengths ≤ 1e5, stops and source/target are in [0, 1e6).

title: Count the Number of Substrings With Dominant Ones
description: Given a binary string s, count how many substrings have number of ones >= (number of zeros)^2. The length of s is up to 4*10^4, so enumerating all O(n^2) substrings is too slow and you should exploit the constraint zeros <= sqrt(n) for dominant substrings.

title: Find Median from Data Stream
description: Maintain a data structure that supports streaming insertion of integers and returning the median at any time. Up to 5*10^4 operations, values in range [-10^5, 10^5], and findMedian is called only when at least one element exists.

complexity.time: addNum: O(log n) per insertion (due to heap operations); findMedian: O(1); total for n insertions O(n log n)
complexity.space: O(n) additional space to store all elements in the two heaps

title: Maximize Subarrays After Removing One Conflicting Pair
description: You have an array nums = [1..n]. Each conflicting pair [a,b] forbids any subarray that contains both a and b. You must remove exactly one conflicting pair and then maximize the number of non-empty subarrays that do not contain any remaining conflicting pair. Constraints: n up to 1e5 and up to 2n conflicting pairs (pairs are between 1 and n).

title: Maximum Palindromes After Operations
description: Given an array of strings, you can swap any characters between any strings arbitrarily; maximize how many strings can be turned into palindromes. Key constraints: n up to 1000, each word length up to 100, and only lowercase letters.

complexity.time: O(T) where T = total number of characters across all words (<= n * maxLen)
complexity.space: O(1) (26-size frequency array plus O(1) extra variables)
